73580-procrustes.title: FUTURE _of_ ENGLISH EDUCATION
73580-procrustes.creator: M. Alderton Pink, M.A.
73580-procrustes.description: A book by M. Alderton Pink, M.A.. These views are certainly extreme; but, looked at impartially, they contain so much plain common-sense that it is rather remarkable that they provoked such bitter opposition. Of course, Lord Hugh Cecil laid himself open to two obvious charges: first, that he had no special knowledge of his subject, and, secondly, that his reforms were presumably intended for the children of masses and not those of his own class.

arxiv-1703-09099.title: (Anti-)BRST and (Anti-)co-BRST Symmetries in 2D non-Abelian Gauge Theory: Some Novel Observations
arxiv-1703-09099.creator: S. Kumar
arxiv-1703-09099.description: Abstract Abstract: We discuss the nilpotent Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin (BRST), anti-BRST and (anti-)co-BRST symmetry transformations and derive their corresponding conserved charges in the case of a two (1+1)-dimensional (2D) self-interacting non-Abelian gauge theory (without any interaction with matter fields). We point out a set of novel features that emerge out in the BRST and co-BRST analysis of the above 2D gauge theory.

arxiv-2208-06703.creator: Esther Ezra, Micha Sharir
arxiv-2208-06703.description: Abstract We develop data structures for intersection queries in four dimensions that involve segments, triangles and tetrahedra. Specifically, we study three main problems: (i) Preprocess a set of n n tetrahedra in ℝ 4 {\mathbb{R}}^{4} into a data structure for answering segment-intersection queries amid the given tetrahedra (referred to as segment-tetrahedron intersection queries ).

arxiv-2210-15429.creator: James Lee Hu*, Mohammadreza Ebrahimi*, Weifeng Li, Xin Li*, Hsinchun Chen
arxiv-2210-15429.description: Abstract Deep learning-based adversarial malware detectors have yielded promising results in detecting never-before-seen malware executables without relying on expensive dynamic behavior analysis and sandbox. Despite their abilities, these detectors have been shown to be vulnerable to adversarial malware variants - meticulously modified, functionality-preserving versions of original malware executables generated by machine learning.

arxiv-2306-06821.title: Towards end-to-end ASP computation
arxiv-2306-06821.creator: Taisuke Sato, Akihiro Takemura, Katsumi Inoue
arxiv-2306-06821.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Taisuke Sato, Akihiro Takemura, Katsumi Inoue. We propose an end-to-end approach for answer set programming (ASP) and linear algebraically compute stable models satisfying given constraints. The idea is to implement Lin-Zhao’s theorem [ 14 ] together with constraints directly in vector spaces as numerical minimization of a cost function constructed from a matricized normal logic program, loop formulas in Lin-Zhao’s theorem and constraints, thereby no use of symbolic ASP or SAT solvers involved in our approach.

arxiv-2402-19181.title: Structure of Periodic Orbit Families in the Hill Restricted 4-Body Problem
arxiv-2402-19181.creator: Gavin M. Brown, Luke T. Peterson, Damennick B. Henry, Daniel J. Scheeres
arxiv-2402-19181.description: Abstract The Hill Restricted 4-Body Problem (HR4BP) is a coherent time-periodic model that can be used to represent motion in the Sun-Earth-Moon (SEM) system. Periodic orbits were computed in this model to better understand the periodic orbit family structures that exist in these types of systems.

arxiv-2412-13892.description: Abstract This paper addresses, for the first time, the uplink performance optimization of multi-user pinching-antenna (PA) systems, recently developed for next-generation wireless networks. By leveraging the unique capabilities of PAs to dynamically configure wireless channels, we focus on maximizing the minimum achievable data rate between devices to achieve a balanced trade-off between throughput and fairness.

arxiv-2509-08109.title: Unstructured to structured: geometric multigrid on complex geometries via domain remapping Thanks: Received… Accepted… Published online on… Recommended by….
arxiv-2509-08109.creator: Nicolas Nytko, Scott MacLachlan, J. David Moulton, Luke N. Olson, Andrew Reisner, Matthew West
arxiv-2509-08109.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nicolas Nytko, Scott MacLachlan, J. David Moulton, Luke N. Olson, Andrew Reisner, Matthew West. For domains that are easily represented by structured meshes, robust geometric multigrid solvers can quickly provide the numerical solution to many discretized elliptic PDEs. However, for complicated domains with unstructured meshes, constructing suitable hierarchies of meshes becomes challenging. We propose a framework for mapping computations from such complex domains to regular computational domains via diffeomorphisms, enabling the use of robust geometric-style multigrid.

pmc-13289110.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Accounting for only 8% of Earth’s land cover, freshwater wetlands remain the foremost contributors to global methane emissions. Yet the microorganisms and processes underlying methane emissions from wetland soils remain poorly understood. Over a five-year period, we surveyed the microbial membership and in situ methane measurements from over 700 samples in one of the most prolific methane-emitting wetlands in the United States.

pmc-13363966.title: A Lightweight Zero-Trust-Based Authentication Framework for UAV Systems
pmc-13363966.creator: Xiang Qu, Wei Ou, Mengxue Pang, Yangbo Chen, Yishan Wu, Qiuling Yue, Wenbao Han
pmc-13363966.description: To address identity cloning, credential leakage, and delayed authorization in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems operating in open airspace, we propose a zero-trust authentication and authorization framework. SM9 identity-based mutual authentication establishes a traceable digital identity anchor. On-demand rotor acoustic verification then checks whether the current platform matches the registered identity.

pmc-13392526.description: BackgroundTaiwan is projected to become a “super-aged” society by 2025, leading to an increasing demand for community psychiatric long-term care (LTC). pmc-13532016.title: Pathogenicity and virulence of Ralstonia solanacearum species complex: Understanding its virulence mechanisms for proper management
pmc-13532016.creator: Masayuki Tsuzuki, Yasufumi Hikichi, Sora Tateda, Akinori Kiba, Kouhei Ohnishi
pmc-13532016.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The soil-borne Gram-negative beta-proteobacterium Ralstonia solanacearum species complex (RSSC) causes bacterial wilt, a devastating plant disease that threatens crop production and food security worldwide. In this review, we first summarize current knowledge of RSSC pathogenicity and virulence, focusing on the factors that determine its ability to infect and cause disease, including advances in resistance breeding and the genetic basis of host resistance to bacterial wilt.

pmc-13588163.title: Divergent drainage-scale responses to lithological heterogeneity
pmc-13588163.creator: Yifei Li, Huiping Zhang, Xudong Zhao, Mikael Attal, Simon M. Mudd, Peizhen Zhang
pmc-13588163.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite widespread recognition that lithological heterogeneity helps shape river networks, a widely applicable topographic diagnostic for whether and where lithological contrasts drive drainage reorganization is still lacking. Here, we introduce a drainage-network metric, the rock proportion–contributing area order (RP-CAO) relationship, and further show that responses diverge with drainage scale: small, low-discharge channels divert around resistant rocks, whereas large, high-discharge rivers largely maintain their course and incise through them.
